user.title: Battery Management
user.description: Pick the household grid-power sensor (+ = import, - = export) and how many battery units to coordinate. You can tune the control parameters later under Configure.

data.bias: Import bias (W) - aim for a small import so you never export
data.deadband: Deadband (W) - ignore errors smaller than this

unit_device.title: Battery unit {index} of {total}: pick the device
unit_device.description: Pick the Anker device for this unit and the next screen is filled in for you - you still get to check it. Leave it empty to select all six entities by hand.

unit.title: Battery unit {index} of {total}
unit.description: Select the Modbus control entities for this Anker SOLIX Max AC unit. The two limit fields are optional and expect a percentage - leave them blank to use 100 % / 5 %.

unit_modes.title: Battery unit: {name} - what its modes mean
unit_modes.description:
This unit offers: {options}.

Pick which one hands control to the coordinator, and which one gives it back when you switch off. Leave the second empty if there is nothing to return to - the unit is then simply commanded 0 W, which is a safe resting state. A pack without its own P1 meter has no self-consumption mode, so this is normal.

data.mode_control: Option that hands control to the coordinator
data.mode_safe: Option to return to when switching off (leave empty to only command 0 W)

error.duplicate_name: Another unit already uses this name. Names must be unique, otherwise the two packs are treated as one.
error.duplicate_entity: This entity is already used for another field on this unit. Each field needs its own entity.
error.limit_not_percentage: This looks like a power entity, not a state-of-charge percentage. The limit fields expect a percentage (0-100); leave blank to use 100 % / 5 %.
error.missing_options: This select does not offer the options the coordinator needs (self_consumption / third_party_control, or charge / discharge). Check the entity, or adjust the option strings in const.py if your firmware renamed them.

tuning.title: Tune the coordinator
tuning.description: Saving reloads the integration. The units are briefly handed back to self-consumption, then the coordinator resumes on its own with the setpoint it had.

data.fast_charge_hold: Keep the packs full after a fast charge (release with the switch)
data.full_charge_minutes: Minutes from empty to full at max power (0 = not measured, hides the estimate)
data.external_timeout: Minutes an external setpoint stays valid before handing control back

units.title: Battery unit {index} of {total}: {name}
units.description: Correct the control entities for this unit. The two limit fields expect a percentage - leave them blank to use 100 % / 5 %.

dynamic.title: Dynamic tariff
dynamic.description: Optional. Without a price sensor the Dynamic mode is not offered and nothing else changes. Exchange (day-ahead) prices are enough: tax and markup shift every hour equally, so the cheap-to-expensive order is the same.

data.price_sensor: Price sensor (any integration publishing upcoming prices)
data.cheap_hours: Hours per day to charge from the grid on
data.charge_below_soc: Only buy when a pack is below this state of charge (%)
data.solar_forecast_max: Skip buying when more sun than this is expected (kWh, 0 = ignore)

shadow.title: Shadow running
shadow.description: Only matters while Dry run is on. Simulating the meter is what makes a shadow comparison honest: without it the other controller is already regulating the meter, so this one sees nothing to do and parks at zero.

data.shadow_simulate: Simulate the meter from reconstructed demand (recommended)
data.battery_power_sensor: Measured battery power, signed, + = discharging (optional; otherwise read back from the target entities)

error.duplicate_name: Another unit already uses this name. Names must be unique, otherwise the two packs are treated as one.
error.duplicate_entity: This entity is already used for another field on this unit. Each field needs its own entity.
error.limit_not_percentage: This looks like a power entity, not a state-of-charge percentage. The limit fields expect a percentage (0-100); leave blank to use 100 % / 5 %.
error.missing_options: This select does not offer the options the coordinator needs (self_consumption / third_party_control, or charge / discharge). Check the entity, or adjust the option strings in const.py if your firmware renamed them.
error.battery_power_is_grid: That is the grid meter, not the batteries. The reconstruction adds the two together, so using the meter here counts it twice and the comparison becomes worthless. Leave this empty unless you have a sensor for the packs' own combined power - empty reads it back from the target entities, which is what you want.

state.deadband: Difference too small to act on
state.external_stale: External plan went quiet, regulating on its own

external_no_plan.title: Smart charging needs an external optimiser
external_no_plan.description:
The coordinator is set to **External plan**, but no plan has arrived in the last {timeout} minutes, so it has handed control back to normal grid-zero regulation.

This mode does not plan anything itself. It executes a plan produced elsewhere — typically **EMHASS**, which optimises against price, solar and load forecasts. EMHASS is a separate project: it is **not** installed with this integration and is not a dependency.

Install and configure it (or any other optimiser), and have it call the `battery_management.set_setpoint` service. Positive discharges, negative charges. This message clears itself as soon as a plan arrives.

Not using an optimiser? Pick a different mode — **Follow the meter** charges from your solar surplus and discharges on demand, with no extra software.
